core_concepts: Acknowledgments So many mentors, partners, colleagues, staff, clients, friends, and adopters of the Getting Things Done methodology around the world over the past decades have contributed to my understanding and devel
In the early 1980s Dean Acheson and Russell Bishop provided me initial frameworks that seeded my awareness of the powerful methodology that was to become known around the world as GTD
It’s not what we have in our life, but who we have in our life, that counts
In addition, many thousands of clients and workshop participants have helped validate and fine-tune these models

This book could not have happened the way it has without the unique energies and perspectives of Tom Hagan, John and Laura McBride, Steve Lewers, Greg Stikeleather, Sam Spurlin, and my indefatigable agent, Doe Coover

Finally, deepest thanks go to my spiritual coach, J-R, for being such an awesome guide and consistent reminder of my real priorities; and to my wife, Kathryn, for her trust, love, supportive hard work, companionship

And much credit is due both the editor of the first edition, Janet Goldstein, and my subsequent editor of this new version, Rick Kot, both of whom have provided marvelous (and patient) instruction in the art and craft
So, my gratitude and apologies go to the many unnamed but still highly deserving in that group (and you know who you are!)

Of the innumerable partners and colleagues who have added to this body of work and its distribution over the years, I must give special thanks to Marian Bateman, Meg Edwards, Ana Maria Gonzalez, Anne Gennett, Leslie B
